clue.text: Roman fort said to be destroyed

parts.note: Deva was the Roman fort and town on the site of modern Chester
said means stated, declared

explanation.surface: A Roman fort is reported to have been razed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a homophone signal, but here it simply means STATED. DEVA is the Roman name for Chester, an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a place laid waste and wrecked is ruined or destroyed.

clue.text: Reveal the age of fruit

explanation.surface: Someone works out how old a piece of fruit is.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal an object's age is to put a year on it, and a sweet palm fruit shares the same name.

clue.text: Country of vigour — something likely to erupt in it?

indicators.note: in it tells us the volcano goes inside the word for vigour

parts.note: vim is energy or vigour
Etna is the active volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: A lively country with a volcano liable to blow at any moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a nation in South-East Asia is a country.

clue.text: Have I not task of an exceptional nature?

definitions.text: Have I not task of an exceptional nature?

indicators.note: exceptional nature suggests the letters of the preceding words are put into an unusual new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the job given to them is not an extraordinary one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a Stakhanovite was a Soviet worker who exceeded production targets, so the speaker's task really is exceptional.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stakhanovite is a hugely productive worker, named after a Soviet miner who mined far beyond his quota.

clue.text: A province getting defeated is lively

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
mated means beaten at chess, so defeated

explanation.surface: A region that has lost is nonetheless full of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: NI stands for Northern Ireland, the UK region traditionally called 'the Province'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something full of life and movement is spirited or lively.

clue.text: Tempt last of the children out with a cornet?

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: a cornet is a cone holding ice cream, here simply ice

explanation.surface: Coaxing the final child outside by offering an ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of the children' reads as the last child, but 'last of' takes the final letters of THE, CHILDREN and OUT: E, N, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lure or coax someone with a bait is to tempt them.

clue.text: Strike marbles on the rebound

indicators.note: on the rebound suggests bouncing back, so the word for marbles is read backwards

parts.note: taws are large marbles used for shooting

explanation.surface: Hitting marbles as they bounce back.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to swipe at with a sharp blow, as at a fly, is to hit or strike.

clue.text: Dispute when right is swamped by devious practice

indicators.note: being swamped by means being engulfed, so the letter for right goes inside the other word

parts.note: a wangle is a crafty or devious trick for getting something

explanation.surface: An argument arises when fair play is overwhelmed by trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a long, noisy argument is a quarrel or dispute.

clue.text: No longer 'igh up in community that's crumbling

indicators.note: in shows the dropped-H word sits inside the word for community

parts.note: a town is a community
humbled means brought low, no longer high up; written with the H dropped, as the Cockney 'igh hints

explanation.surface: A Cockney laments that someone has come down in the world in a decaying neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'igh shows a dropped H, Cockney (London) style, so HUMBLED loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a building falling to pieces is dilapidated or crumbling.

clue.text: Healers and believers absorbing criticism

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the word for believers holds the word for criticism

parts.note: theists are those who believe in God
rap means blame or criticism, as in take the rap

explanation.surface: Healers and the faithful take criticism on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: practitioners treating illness or distress are healers.

clue.text: A bit of a hand will be needed to bring victory

explanation.surface: A small part of a card hand might be what wins the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner surface of the hand is one sense; a frond of the tree was the ancient token of triumph, hence victory.

clue.text: Lab team has to disrupt a blood cell

indicators.note: disrupt means throw into disorder, so the letters of lab team has to are scrambled

explanation.surface: A laboratory team must break up a blood cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' belongs to the anagram fodder as well as reading naturally before 'disrupt'; the indicator is 'disrupt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A haematoblast is a primitive cell from which blood cells develop, so it is a type of blood cell.

clue.text: Island's measure of precipitation

definitions.meaning: a small Scottish or Irish island, as in Inchcolm; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: An island's rainfall measured.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland and Ireland a small island is called an inch; rainfall is also measured in inches.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gaelic-derived word for a small island; also a unit of length used to record rainfall.

clue.text: A tanker finally given modification left port

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word tanker

parts.note: a modification is a change

explanation.surface: A tanker, finally altered, departed the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left port' reads as 'departed the harbour', but 'port' is the definition: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a Russian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Archangel is a Russian seaport on the White Sea.

clue.text: Meet viper moving round python's head, with intent to disable enemy

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the python's first letter
moving signals the letters of meet viper are shifted into a new order
head points to the first letter of python

explanation.surface: Snakes meet; one circles the python's head to disable it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges MEET VIPER and 'round' puts them around P, the head of 'python'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-emptive strike is made in advance to cripple a foe before it can act.

clue.text: Nudge bodyguard after Queen's returned

indicators.note: after places the bodyguard word behind the turned letters
returned means turned back, so the Queen's letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
a minder is a bodyguard

explanation.surface: A bodyguard gets a prod once the Queen is back.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; 'Nudge' suits a prod to the memory, not a shove.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a prompt jogging the memory is a nudge.

clue.text: Mischief-maker with purpose to be threatening

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or sprite
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A troublemaker with a goal is menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hang over as a looming danger is to threaten.

clue.text: One man is taken in by another making superficial gestures

indicators.note: taken in by means enclosed, so the first man and is go inside the second name

parts.note: Tom is another man's name
Ken is a man's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: One man is duped by another, whose gestures are superficial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like 'deceived', but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokenism is the practice of doing the minimum for show, so it amounts to empty gestures.

clue.text: Plant may be eaten but only the, outside bits go down

indicators.note: only the outside bits means taking just the first and last letters of eaten

parts.note: to dive is to go down

explanation.surface: A plant can be eaten, though only its outer leaves are swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten' seems part of the salad picture, but only its first and last letters, E and N, are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a leafy salad vegetable of the chicory family is a plant.

clue.text: Peace descends with these wild animals?

parts.note: peace comes when the noise departs: din plus goes

explanation.surface: Calm settles in the company of wild animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Peace descends when the din goes; read as two words the answer gives that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingoes are wild Australian dogs, the untamed creatures of the outback.

clue.text: Pugilist taking an unorthodox whop at us

indicators.note: unorthodox means unconventional, so the letters of whop at us are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer takes an unconventional swing at us.
explanation.walkthrough: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer, who leads with the right — itself an unorthodox stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a left-handed boxer is a pugilist.

clue.text: One in 10?

parts.note: the person who lives at Number 10 Downing Street, the British head of government, not a tenth of anything

explanation.surface: A question about a fraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's official residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prime Minister, head of the UK government, lives at Number 10 Downing Street.

clue.text: One getting try in rugby runs with unswerving precision

indicators.note: in places one and try inside the rugby letters

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
I is the Roman numeral one
a go is a try or attempt
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A player scoring a try in rugby runs with total accuracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' and 'runs' look like rugby terms, but 'try' is GO, an attempt, and 'runs' is R, the cricket scorecard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: strict exactness or thoroughness is rigour.

clue.text: Fabric that's the reverse of a bargain — rubbish!

indicators.note: the reverse of means the bargain word is read backwards

parts.note: a snip is a bargain, a cheap buy
tripe means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A fabric that's anything but a bargain is dismissed as junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripe is cloth woven with fine stripes, typical of business suits.

clue.text: Worker goes to river for a drink '

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A worker heads to the river for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ale or lager brewed from malt is a drink.

clue.text: Eve's first young lady to turn up for Adam

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, that is backwards
first points to the first letter of Eve

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young lady entering society

explanation.surface: Eve's first young lady appears instead of Adam.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Bede is George Eliot's novel, so BEDE is the name that goes with Adam. 'to turn up' reverses E + DEB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bede is the surname of Adam, hero of George Eliot's novel of that title.

clue.text: One prisoner becoming a holy figure?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A convict turns into a saintly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a religious image of a saint painted on wood is a sacred figure.

clue.text: Local inhabitant without honour in a case

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the inhabitant word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a native is someone born in the place
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A local person lacking a decoration is in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside, an old sense; 'case' is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the subject form of a noun is called a case.

clue.text: One of four at table to have big meal, not the first

indicators.note: not the first means its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to feast is to eat a large meal

explanation.surface: One of four diners can't be the first to tuck into a feast.
explanation.walkthrough: At the bridge table the four players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four seats are compass points, so one player sits at one of them.

clue.text: Master's piercing exclamation of annoyance, getting push from theatrical type

indicators.note: piercing means stabbing into, so the degree letters go inside the curse

parts.note: drat is a mild curse
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree
to urge is to push or press

explanation.surface: A master gives a shrill cry of annoyance as a stagey person shoves him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piercing' reads as 'shrill', but it is the container signal; MA is Master of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramaturge is a playwright or literary adviser to a theatre, a theatre professional.
